verdict.rationale: LightSprint documents connecting your own repository, says its onboarding agent sets up the codebase, environment variables and setup script automatically, and claims GitHub workflows work out of the box with permissions inherited from GitHub. That supports low-friction repo access, but there is no evidence of a one-click install flow. The 'one click' claim on the skills page is about adding skills, not granting repo access, so it is not credited. Missing for 10: a documented one-click repo install or GitHub App authorization flow, step-by-step detail on how repo access is granted and scoped, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the setup experience.

support.subject: As a developer, I can grant an agent access to my repositories with a one-click install, without complex setup

citations.quote: Connect a starter app or your own repository.
LightSprint's onboarding agent will set up your codebase, environment variables and setup script automatically.
GitHub-backed delivery: branch rules, required reviews, GitHub Actions, and merge queues work out of the box.
Permissions follow the merge authority settings on Github. Roles map to your existing org structure - no new permissions model to build.
